lines.trans: Did you have a nice rest? Where did you go?
Thanks to you, yes—I was staying with friends.
Do you actually have friends whom I do not know about?
I have friends too—please do not ask any further; since I came back safely, is that not enough?
If you and I go to war, you are guaranteed to lose—and I did not raise you foolish enough to miss that.
I know that too—yet how could a war like that break out so easily?
I am asset number one on your balance sheet—you hate the idea of losing me too, CEO.
Smart as ever, our Cindy—except Cindy, I have already lost a star like you once before.
She was just as precious to me as you are—yet right after I lost her, you came along, remember?
If you disappear, your spot will be filled right away too.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.

meanings.note: Used as conjunction (그렇지만).

examples.text: 역시 우리 신디는 똑똑해. 그렇지만 신디야, 난 잃어봤단다.
examples.trans: Smart as ever, our Cindy—except Cindy, I have already lost a star like you once before.

examples.text: 너처럼 나한텐 소중한 아이였어. 그렇지만 그 아이를 잃고 나니까 네가 왔잖니?
examples.trans: She was just as precious to me as you are—yet right after I lost her, you came along, remember?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: With future or present-progressive verbs, means 'right away / in a moment'.
With past-tense verbs, means 'just now'.

examples.trans: I'll be right there.
I just arrived a moment ago.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.
Test
Test2

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to express gratitude for someone's help.

examples.trans: Thanks to you, I'm doing well.
It is all thanks to the teacher.

meanings.note: Used as past causal (돌아왔으니까).

examples.text: 있어요 나도, 친구들. 더 이상은 안 물어보셨으면 좋겠어요, 어쨌든 잘 돌아왔으니까 된 거 아니에요?
examples.trans: I have friends too—please do not ask any further; since I came back safely, is that not enough?
Let us do that (returned, so) right away.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Used as casual present (똑똑해.).

examples.text: 역시 우리 신디는 똑똑해. 그렇지만 신디야, 난 잃어봤단다.
examples.trans: Smart as ever, our Cindy—except Cindy, I have already lost a star like you once before.
It is really is smart compared to what I expected.
Eat as much as you want.
Results will come out as much as you've tried.

meanings.note: Used as adverbial -게 (멍청하게).

examples.text: 너랑 내가 전쟁을 하면 네가 무조건 지게 돼 있어. 그것도 모를 만큼 멍청하게 키우진 않았는데.
examples.trans: If you and I go to war, you are guaranteed to lose—and I did not raise you foolish enough to miss that.
It is really foolishly compared to what I expected.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

examples.text: 노트북? 헤드폰? 다 필요 없어요. 차에선 무조건 잘 거예요.
examples.trans: A laptop? Headphones? You need none of those. You will sleep nonstop in the van.

examples.text: 무조건 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (without fail, unconditionally), we will get good results.
I want to ask right now.
How about trying to ask together tomorrow?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used as adnominal (소중한).

examples.text: 너처럼 나한텐 소중한 아이였어. 그렇지만 그 아이를 잃고 나니까 네가 왔잖니?
examples.trans: She was just as precious to me as you are—yet right after I lost her, you came along, remember?
It is really precious compared to what I expected.

examples.text: 말을 잘 못 알아들으시네. 신디 이번 주 쉬죠?
examples.trans: You are not catching my meaning. Let's have Cindy rest this week, shall we?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 쉬다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (take a break, rest).

meanings.note: ㅂ-irregular adjective (쉽다 -> 쉬워요)

examples.trans: This problem is really easy.

examples.text: 새로운 언어를 배우는 건 쉽지 않아요.
examples.trans: Learning a new language isn't easy.

meanings.note: Descriptive verb (adjective); the thing disliked takes the subject marker 이/가.

examples.trans: I really dislike rainy days.
You hate waking up early in the morning, right?

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.
Aw, really!
Oh, what a surprise.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?

meanings.note: Used to change the subject or brush off previous points.

examples.trans: Anyway, thank you.
I will try it anyway.

없어지다.gloss: to disappear, vanish; to be cancelled

meanings.note: something ceases to exist or be present
used for shows, programs, or policies being discontinued

examples.trans: The key that was on the desk disappeared.
That program was cancelled last year.

examples.text: 역시 아줌마는 사람 속 뒤집어 놓으시는 게 프로야.
examples.trans: As expected, she is a total pro at turning a person's stomach upside down.

examples.text: 역시 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (as expected), we will get good results.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used in negative sentences to mean 'not anymore' or 'no longer'.

examples.trans: I can't do it anymore.
It's beyond expectations.

meanings.note: Used as nominalized -기 (잃기).

examples.text: 대표님 재산목록 1호가 난데 나 잃기 싫잖아요, 대표님도.
examples.trans: I am asset number one on your balance sheet—you hate the idea of losing me too, CEO.

examples.text: 너처럼 나한텐 소중한 아이였어. 그렇지만 그 아이를 잃고 나니까 네가 왔잖니?
examples.trans: She was just as precious to me as you are—yet right after I lost her, you came along, remember?

meanings.note: Used as past declarative -단다 (잃어봤단다.).

examples.text: 역시 우리 신디는 똑똑해. 그렇지만 신디야, 난 잃어봤단다.
examples.trans: Smart as ever, our Cindy—except Cindy, I have already lost a star like you once before.
Let us do that (have lost one before) right away.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: There are no seats.
It's my seat.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.note: Used as compound noun (재산목록).

examples.text: 대표님 재산목록 1호가 난데 나 잃기 싫잖아요, 대표님도.
examples.trans: I am asset number one on your balance sheet—you hate the idea of losing me too, CEO.
This point about asset list, prized possession is really important.

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (전쟁을).

examples.text: 너랑 내가 전쟁을 하면 네가 무조건 지게 돼 있어. 그것도 모를 만큼 멍청하게 키우진 않았는데.
examples.trans: If you and I go to war, you are guaranteed to lose—and I did not raise you foolish enough to miss that.

examples.text: 알아요 나도, 근데 그 전쟁이 어디 쉽게 나겠어요?
examples.trans: I know that too—yet how could a war like that break out so easily?

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

examples.text: 저 가위 낼게요. 안 내면 진 거, 가위바위보!
examples.trans: I am going to throw scissors. Lose if you don't throw—rock, paper, scissors!

examples.text: 가위바위보 해서 져서 내가 하루 종일 들고 다니는 걸로 찍혔잖아요.
examples.trans: I lost rock-paper-scissors and was already filmed carrying them all day.

meanings.note: Used as passive prospective adnominal (채워질).

examples.text: 네가 없어지면 네 자리 역시 금방 채워질 거야.
examples.trans: If you disappear, your spot will be filled right away too.
Let us do that (be filled) right away.

meanings.note: Primary meaning: a friend or peer.

meanings.en: that person / kid (referring to someone younger)
meanings.note: Older speakers often refer to a younger person or celebrity as 그 친구.

examples.trans: I watched a movie with a friend today.
That kid really sings well.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 우리 신디 13살 때부터 내가 키웠는데 처음으로 자기가 하고 싶다고 한 거예요, 이게.
examples.trans: I raised our Cindy since she was thirteen, and this show is the very first thing she ever asked to do herself.
This expression comes from 'raised her, and'.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Bound noun used after Sino-Korean numerals for alert levels, rooms, or lines

examples.trans: My room is number 502.
Typhoon No. 1 is moving north.
